text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The arrival of 7.9 million litres of fuel in Nigeria's commercial capital Lagos is unable to prevent shortages at many filling stations. In other parts of the country the scarcity of fuel is even more severe.

- The Insurance Industry Advisory Council has made a formal request to government for deregulation of the industry and for the scrapping of the law which makes the insurance of government property the responsibility of the state-run National Insurance Company of Nigeria (NICON).
- Leaders of the Ijaw ethnic group, the largest in the oil- producing Niger Delta, have advised the government not to undermine them.
- Seven Up Bottling Company proposes a 200 million naira bottling plant for southeastern Rivers State. The proposal comes as part of expansion plans which follow a drop in turnover last year.
- Anxiety spreads over the health of maverick Afrobeat singer Fela Anikulapo-Kuti.
- Nigerian Stock Exchange criticises the recommendations of a government panel which said a new stock exchange should be established in the new capital Abuja.
- National Reconciliation Committee schedules fresh talks with the Ogoni community from oil-producing southeast Nigeria.
- A price war between Sudan and Chad in the gum arabic market has cost Nigerian producers at least $6 million through lower prices, a large exporter says.
